title: iM Securities lifts GS E&C target as Korea housing recovers and AI DCs spur growth - Chosunbiz
content: iM Securities said on the 2nd that GS Engineering & Construction(006360) has entered a phase of normalization in its core business, helped by a gradual recovery in the dwellings institutional sector and new growth momentum such as the Donghae artificial intelligence (AI) data center (DC). It maintained its "buy" recommendation and raised the target price to 38,000 won from the previous 35,000 won. The previous trading day's closing price was 26,000 won. iM Securities said it derived the target price by applying a target price-to-book ratio (P/B) of 0.70 times to the 12-month forward book value per share (BPS). It noted that it raised the target price-to-book ratio to 0.70 times from 0.65 times to reflect normalization in the dwellings institutional sector and new growth momentum from data centers. On a consolidation basis in the third quarter this year, GS Engineering & Construction posted revenue of 2.744 trillion won, down 14.5% from a year earlier, and operating profit of 95.5 billion won, down 35.7%. This was below the market consensus. While the building and dwellings institutional sectors maintained solid profitability, a combined one-off expense of about 60 billion won was reflected in the plant and infrastructure institutional sectors. In the plant institutional sector, an expected expense of 21.8 billion won related to the delay in completing the Yanbu project in Saudi Arabia was reflected, and in the infrastructure institutional sector, about 38 billion won in expense from the NEL project in Australia was recognized preemptively. However, as new presales increase, it is being assessed that a foundation is being laid for a recovery in dwellings revenue. Cumulative presales volume in the third quarter this year came to 13,744 units, achieving 96% of the guidance at the start of the year. The annual total presales volume is projected to be around 16,700 units, up 86% from about 9,000 units a year earlier. iM Securities said this expansion in presales volume will lead to increased building and dwellings revenue from next year onward. Financial burdens are also easing. Excluding lease liabilities, borrowing fund decreased by about 700 billion won from 6.1 trillion won at the end of last year to 5.4 trillion won at the end of the third quarter this year, helped by solid cash flow and factors such as a decline in the won-dollar exchange rate. As a mid- to long-term growth engine, the Donghae AI data center project is being cited. GS Engineering & Construction won about 250 billion won in orders for transmission and substation infrastructure work to bring in power and is carrying out the project. Procurement for pile and earthwork on the initial 100-megawatt (MW) site is also imminent. The iM Securities research center said, "Groundbreaking for the main construction is expected in early next year, and if it is gradually expanded to 1.2 gigawatts (GW), which is the GS Group's AI DC phase 01 plan, the mid- to long-term order and revenue base could expand significantly." GS Caltex GS Caltex announced on November 2 that Kixx Prime was named No. 1 in the premium gasoline category of the 2026 Korea Quality Satisfaction Index (KS-QEI), organized by the Korean Standards Association, following its win last year. GS Caltex said it has strengthened its competitiveness in the premium fuel market through continuous technological development and quality management since launching Kixx Prime in April 2006. Depending on the vehicle's characteristics, it provides smooth acceleration and a quiet driving experience. In particular, it contains high-performance engine detergents and friction reducers, which help manage contaminants inside the engine and reduce energy loss caused by friction. GS Caltex verifies the product's quality and reliability through collaboration and testing with various high-performance vehicle manufacturers. It also operates a management system to maintain consistent quality throughout the entire process, from raw material procurement to production and supply. GS Caltex plans to continue strengthening its competitiveness in the premium fuel market through research and development and quality innovation. Kim Changsu, head of GS Caltex's Mobility & Marketing Division, said, "Kixx Prime's selection as No. 1 in the premium gasoline category of the Korea Quality Satisfaction Index for the second consecutive year is a meaningful achievement made possible by our continuous efforts to improve quality and the trust of our customers. One useful way to value a bank is to compare the return it generates on equity with its cost of equity, which represents the return owners require for taking on risk. When a bank consistently produces returns above that cost, it creates value beyond its book value. Goldman Sachs' average return on equity sits well above its estimated cost of equity, indicating that each dollar of owner capital is producing a meaningful surplus. An excess returns model builds on that idea by estimating the surplus Goldman Sachs generates above its cost of equity and projecting how long that surplus can last. title: Becky G might be the all-time best gift-giver — these are her top picks for this holiday season - NBC News
content: Becky G doesn’t play around with holiday gifts — here’s what she’s giving the lucky people in her life this season NBC Selected independently determines what we cover and recommend. When you click on or buy through our links, we earn a commission. Learn more. Talking Shop is our series where we talk to interesting people about their most interesting buys. Becky G has been going nonstop all year. Not only did the singer release her fifth studio album, Baraja Bendita, which was nominated for Top Latin Pop Album of the Year at the 2026 Billboard Latin Music Awards, but she also filmed a new movie and led a cross-country headlining tour. She also helped Patrón design a limited-edition “Our Rainwater Project” bottle, which funded 200 rainwater harvesting systems for households in Jalisco, Mexico. Needless to say, the L.A.-based superstar is ready for some much-needed rest and relaxation this holiday season. “I’ve been away from home a lot more this year. I’ve definitely been putting my head down and grinding it out, so I’m looking forward to family time — celebrating with them, reconnecting, and eating some yummy food,” says Becky G. “It’ll be a fun holiday, for sure.” In addition to making her family’s annual tamales, she’s preparing for Las Posadas, a nine-day religious celebration that takes place from December 16 to December 24, and readying her holiday shopping list. “I’m really big on gift giving,” she says. “It’s my favorite time of the year to catch up with everybody and give them things that I’ve put a lot of thought into.” She adds that, regardless of presents and parties, showing up and celebrating together is the most important part of the holiday season. “Now more than ever, there’s a unity that we need as a community and a time that we need with our family. It’s a beautiful reminder of what really matters in life.” Below, Becky G breaks down the gifts on her holiday shopping list this year, including a white elephant gift everyone will fight over and useful stocking stuffers. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Becky G describes herself as ritualistic when it comes to her pre-show routines — and restocks of her go-to essentials are always appreciated around the holidays. “I always have to have palo santo and sage,” she says. “I’m really big on essence sprays and things that cleanse the space. It’s very helpful for me to set the vibes. I’m a vibe curator, so I would say those are things that I absolutely love receiving.” Lé Trois Apothecary offers three essential oil ritual cleansers: one for relaxation and release, one for manifestation, and one for grounding. The brand’s No. 3 cleanser to create unity and connection was inspired by Becky G and it features notes of bergamot, oud, and vetiver. Not one to miss her family’s white elephant gift exchange, Becky G says a bottle of Patrón Tequila was one of the best presents she’s ever brought. “It was the hot ticket item that everybody was battling it out for, and at the end, people started linking up with other people to trade gifts to get it.” An official partner of the brand, she recently designed an exclusive bottle for the Rainwater Project, which helped bring 200 rainwater harvesting systems to families in Jalisco, Mexico. A fan of buying and gifting things with intention, Becky G is planning on giving friends a bottle from that collection this year because it’s a present that’s connected to something close to her heart. “When I’ve been given things that are for the community and for the culture, it hits me differently and it reminds me that we’re a part of something bigger and it makes me want to do the same,” she says. Patrón silver tequila is an unaged blanco tequila made from 100% Weber Blue Agave. You must be 21+ to purchase and consume. If someone came up to Becky G and asked her for a mid-luxury beauty product to give as a gift, she’d recommend Dezi Skin’s Agua Fresca Moisturizer. “Desi Perkins killed it with Dezi Skin; there’s not one product that I do not love, especially Pore Choices, the new mist she just released. But, the OG Agua Fresca moisturizer is also incredible,” she says. The fragrance-free gel-cream moisturizer is formulated with niacinamide, hyaluronic acid and antioxidants to help give skin a much-needed boost of hydration. It’s lightweight and can be used with all skin types to help target fine lines, dryness and elasticity. Every year, Becky G likes to give her team presents that they can make together. Last year, she bought them a Mexican coffee set from a small cafe in Los Angeles. The kit included the coffeehouse’s signature Café de Olla — a traditional Mexican coffee brewed with ground cinnamon and piloncillo (unrefined Mexican sugar) — and a bag of Oaxaca Reserve beans. “Little thoughtful things like that are super, super fun to put together,” she says. Traditionally, café de olla is made in a clay pot, which imbues the coffee with more flavor. While you can make café de olla in a regular saucepan, you can also purchase an olla for less than $40 on Etsy — just make sure to wash it by hand with warm water and baking soda (or coarse salt) when you’re done. Chemical-based detergents are easily absorbed into the clay and can give your food (and coffee) a soapy taste. One thing about Becky G is she commits to an aesthetic. Each of her family members gets a matching color scheme for the holidays that’s themed to their personalities, which she helps curate on Etsy. “I get down on wrapping presents. That’s the one thing I enjoy,” she says, noting that she’s usually the one going around and saving the tissue paper and unripped bags. “There’s some bags that have been around at my Christmas for eight years now. We can’t just use these once, come on.” As someone who’s always traveling, Becky G loves tin candles, and she thinks they make a great addition to any stocking. “Tin candles help make a room feel a little more custom to your vibe,” she says. “They’re usually a little bit more potent in scent, so you don’t need to leave them [burning] for a very long time.” During the holidays, she opts for scents like apple cinnamon, which she says reminds her of her mom’s house, and pine. One of her go-to candle brands is Soy Latina Candles, a non-toxic soy candle brand that offers scents inspired by the owner’s Latina heritage. Another of Becky G’s go-to stocking stuffer ideas is anything practical that can be kept in a glove box, like individually packed hand wipes, silk hair ties and lip balm. “I be doing too much with the stockings sometimes. I’m like, it’s overflowing at this point,” she says. I’m a newsletter editor at NBC Selected. title: A magical moment for the Massa Local Police Gs runners. Pieroni storms the Big Apple. Alessandroni and Sartori take center stage. - Quotidiano Sportivo
content: Un periodo di straordinarie soddisfazioni ed emozioni per il Gruppo Sportivo Polizia Locale di Massa, protagonista assoluto su più fronti... A period of extraordinary satisfaction and excitement for the Massa Local Police Sports Group , a key player on multiple fronts, including challenging trails, national championships, and prestigious international stages. In recent days, in the second stage of the Sporteleon Urban Trail circuit in Vezzano Ligure, Silvia Helene Alessandroni achieved a brilliant 4th place overall among the women and 1st place in her category. The athlete from Massa completed the challenging 11,6 km course with over 500 meters of elevation gain in 1 hour 10 minutes and 10 seconds, averaging 6:16 minutes per kilometer along trails, dirt roads, and steps through the villages. On the same day, in Arezzo, Marco Sartori stood out in the 10,6 km half marathon race, valid for the Italian Insurance and Banking Championships . Sartori earned a prestigious third place in the SM70 category, climbing onto the Italian podium, crowning a solid and expertly managed performance. Attention now shifts overseas to today's New York Marathon . Simone Pieroni will tackle the famous 42,195 km in the Big Apple and will have the unique honor of representing Italy in the solemn "Parade of Nations," which opens the race weekend. This significant recognition fills the local police and the entire community of Massa with pride, ready to cheer on their champion from afar on a global stage. title: GS Caltex's Balanced Attack Secures Opening Match Victory - 조선일보
content: Evolved offense distributes scoring load as Silva, Kwon Minji, Tanacha shine after championship and cup triumphs [Jangchung=Sports Chosun Reporter Lee Jong-seo] "There are parts where Silva has become more comfortable." GS Caltex began the season as the 'defending champion.' Last season, they defeated Korea Expressway Corporation in the championship finals to claim the top spot for the first time in five years. The momentum continued. In the Yeosu Cup final, which concluded last October, they faced Korea Expressway Corporation again and secured victory after a full-set battle. This marked their seventh cup tournament title in team history. They faced Korea Expressway Corporation again in the opening match after about two weeks. This time, GS Caltex smiled again. Silva scored 27 points with a 60% attack success rate, while Tanacha (13 points) and Kwon Minji (11 points) added firepower. Ultimately, they won the opening match held at home with a set score of 3-0 (25-18, 25-21, 25-22). After the match, GS Caltex head coach Lee Young-taek smiled and said, "We won 3-0, so we did very well." The victory was significant, but the team also showcased an elevated level of performance compared to last season. Last season, GS Caltex was often called 'Silva Caltex' due to their heavy reliance on foreign player Silva. Her attack share sometimes exceeded 50%. However, in the first set of this match, Silva's attack share was only 35.14%. Meanwhile, Kwon Minji and Tanacha each took 24.32% of the attack share. Although Silva's share increased in the second and third sets, it did not exceed 50%. With attacks distributed, Silva demonstrated her power with an attack efficiency of 52.5%. Above all, Kwon Minji's growth stood out. In the Yeosu Cup final, she scored 24 points with a 62.86% attack success rate, proving her clear progress. Coach Lee said, "She has a lot of potential. After the championship finals last season, she found confidence. In the cup tournament, she showed some instability early on but performed remarkably in the final. She is in a good rhythm, and that momentum seems to have carried over to the opening match." The addition of Tanacha is also reassuring. Setter Kim Ji-won explained the synergy, saying, "After May (Tanacha's nickname) joined, we became stronger with a triangular formation, so we practiced quick attacks a lot with the two middle blockers." Setter Kim Ji-won is also evaluated as having taken a step forward. Coach Lee said, "Setter Kim Ji-won managed the distribution well. Because of this, Silva could play more comfortably. She is always marked, but there were situations with one-block and one-and-a-half-block defenses. There are parts where Silva has become more comfortable. While it's important for outside hitters to break through, mixing central attacks with stable reception allowed for diverse plays." Although the team now has elements to score from various positions, Silva's consistent performance remains the biggest pillar. Kim Ji-won said, "I think we have a reliable attacker. When the score is close, she can secure points decisively." Coach Lee also expressed firm trust in Silva, saying, "We have to use her when needed. Although Silva is a year older, she is managing herself well. This is her fourth season with us. We have a manual for her." He added, "If she maintains this, she will be able to perform well until the end."

title: -100 kg: Bifov Climbs to the Top of the Podium - IJF
content: This was an explosive contest that looked to be heading France’s way. Aurelien Diesse had energy and dynamic movement and he seemed unfired to attack. He scored a yuko after 90 seconds had passed but during the same exchange, Bifov took the advantage and turned a deficit into a win, armlocking Diesse. From his place at 129th in the world ranking, Diesse can be proud of his new sil ver medal but the crown is Bifov’s today, his second grand slam gold. After the final, Idar Bifov said, “I feel joy and happiness. The first bout was harder than the final but I managed to win the gold medal this year in Abu Dhabi, just like last year. Before the final, we analysed the Frenchman's previous match and my coach helped me prepare, pointeing out the mistakes I needed to avoid.” Bronze medal contest: Zsombor Veg (HUN) vs Anton Savytskiy (UKR) Zsombor Veg had a fantastic morning session and looked to be working with momentum in the final block, but for a single moment of inspire judo from Anton Savytskiy who launched a seoi-otoshi under him to score a yuko just 37 seconds before the end of the contest. Unable to make up the shortfall in such a short time, Veg had to settle for 5th place. Anton Savytskiy now has his ninth World Judo Tour medal, a career that is really beginning to take shape. title: +78 kg: Victory for Vukovic - IJF
content: Helena Vukovic gripped excellently to neutralise Hershko’s usual attacks but Raz has other strings to her bow. She began to mix up the techniques, adding ashi-waza to the mix and coming close to taking a lead just a minute before the end. Hershko, the favourite, had a new silver medal, while Helena Vukovic, having played an excellent strategy, had her first grand slam gold medal. “I’m feeling really happy with my first grand slam gold medal, especially after getting my first win over an amazing opponent, staying focused and executing our tactics,” said Helena Vukovic. “It lifts a huge weight off my shoulders to start my Olympic qualification with such a strong result. title: -78 kg: Lytvynenko Leads Again - IJF
content: FInal: Yelyzaveta Lytvynenko (UAE) vs Patricia Sampaio (POR) The world number two and world number five delivered an exceptionally high level final, one that was balancing on a knife edge. With either judoka poised to claim the win at any moment, furious attacks coming from white and blue, the volume rose in the Mubadala Arena. After two minutes of extra time Sampaio had two penalties and Lytvynenko had one but there were spells of dominance from both. However, a minute later, Sampaio attacked with a seoi-otoshi that lacked a little movement and Lytvynenko capitalised, countering for a waza-ari and the gold. This is a perfect finish for the host nation, a gold medal on the third and final day of competition in Abu Dhabi. “I feel good, said Lytvynenko, “I’m tired but I'm happy because it feels like home and I am so glad to win a gold medal for my country. title: Defending Champions GS Caltex Secure Home Opener Shutout - 조선일보
content: Team defeats Korea Expressway Corporation 3-0 in first match under new official coach Kim Young-rae [Jangchung=Sports Chosun Reporter Lee Jong-seo] GS Caltex secured a thrilling 'shutout' victory in their home opener. GS Caltex defeated Korea Expressway Corporation 3-0 (25-18, 25-21, 25-22) in the HK Savings Bank 2026-2027 V-League Women’s Division match held at Jangchung Gymnasium on the 31st. The two teams, which clashed in last season’s championship finals and this year’s cup tournament final, were both victorious in those encounters. The winner of the season opener was GS Caltex. Silva unleashed a fierce attack, while Kwon Min-ji and Thanacha provided solid firepower support. Korea Expressway Corporation fought hard with Moma, but failed to prevent the defeat. Before the match, GS Caltex head coach Lee Young-taek said, “Korea Expressway Corporation is a well-organized and strong team. I expect a tough game. We won the last match (the cup tournament) and are in good form. I hope the players will perform like they did in the finals.” This was Korea Expressway Corporation’s first match under head coach Kim Young-rae, who has shed the ‘acting’ tag and been officially appointed. Before the game, Coach Kim said, “I’m very nervous. I’m also excited. I’ve prepared well, so I’ll try to help the players perform their best. It’s much more nerve-wracking (being the official coach). The first step is the most important. It’s the start of the season and my first match as head coach. I’m very tense. Still, I trust my players.” In sets one and two, GS Caltex dominated. Silva recorded an attack success rate of over 60%, scoring 8 and 11 points respectively. Korea Expressway Corporation made no major unforced errors but struggled to keep up, passively conceding points throughout. In the early stages of the third set, Korea Expressway Corporation showed strength, diverging from the previous two sets. Mami extended the lead with consecutive attack points and a block point. They opened a 5-point gap at 16-11, but GS Caltex demonstrated strong resilience. Silva’s attacks were complemented by Thanacha’s quick open spikes and successful blocks. Ultimately, Silva’s back-row attack tied the score at 17-17. In the end, GS Caltex prevailed. After Moma’s attacks went out of bounds consecutively at 21-21, they took a 23-21 lead. They secured the match and celebrated their season-opening victory.

title: Karnataka Rajyotsava Award row: Outrage over withdrawal of Dr G S Chandrashekar’s name - Daijiworld
content:
Udupi, Oct 31: The Karnataka government's decision to withdraw the Rajyotsava Award announced for renowned Udupi-based physician Dr G S Chandrashekar has sparked widespread criticism, with citizens, medical professionals and various organisations expressing strong displeasure over the move. Dr G S Chandrashekar, medical director of Udupi's reputed Adarsha Hospital, was initially named among the recipients of this year's Karnataka Rajyotsava Awards. However, in a subsequent development, his name was removed from the list, reportedly citing technical reasons. The decision has come as a shock to many in Udupi, particularly considering Dr Chandrashekar's contributions to the healthcare sector. He has dedicated more than three decades to providing selfless medical services to the people of Udupi and has earned widespread recognition for his commitment to patient care and public service. The government's move has raised questions over the selection process, with many questioning why an award was announced in the first place if there were technical issues that warranted his exclusion. Adding to the controversy, the government had announced a Rajyotsava Award recipient from Uttara Kannada district, while Dr Chandrashekar's name from Udupi was subsequently withdrawn. The decision has triggered strong reactions from the medical fraternity, various organisations and members of the public, who have expressed disappointment and demanded clarity from the state government. Many believe that Dr Chandrashekar's decades-long contribution to society deserves recognition and have urged the government to reconsider its decision. Dr P V Bhandary questions withdrawal, seeks reinstatement of award In a statement, Dr P V Bhandary, renowned psychiatrist and social worker of Udupi said that the issue was merely a district-name error and could have been corrected through a simple amendment rather than withdrawing the award altogether. Recalling his professional association with Dr Chandrashekar during their service at a government hospital, Dr Bhandary said he had personally witnessed the latter's commitment to medical service. He pointed out that Dr Chandrashekar has been responding to emergency calls at any hour, irrespective of a patient's identity or financial background, and has continued such selfless service for nearly three decades. "An administrative mistake should be corrected by the concerned department. A person who has done no wrong should not have to pay the price for it," Dr Bhandary stated. Clarifying that he had no objection to the selection of G U Bhat, whose name was subsequently included in the award list, Dr Bhandary said his appeal was solely to ensure justice for Dr Chandrashekar. He urged the Karnataka and Udupi branches of the Indian Medical Association (IMA) to submit an official protest to the government. He also appealed to the chief minister and the department of Kannada and Culture to reinstate the Rajyotsava Award announced for Dr Chandrashekar, with Udupi district correctly mentioned. Dr G S Chandrashekar is the right person, government should correct its mistake - Ansar Ahmed Speaking exclusively with Daijiworld.com Ansar Ahmed, a social worker, stated, "Dr G S Chandrashekar is the right person for the Rajyotsava Award." It is a shame for the government to announce the award and then again to take it back. Dr G S Chandrashekar has rendered selfless service for the district for over 30 years. He is the only person who would overcome any difficulty and render his service even at 12 am if required. I have witnessed his selfless service in many occasions. It was the government's mistake, and the government should correct it themselves. I urge the state government to reinstate the award declared for Dr G S Chandrashekar. It is a dishonour done to the professional healthcare community." Meanwhile, Umesh A Naik of Cherkady has also strongly criticised the government's decision, stating that such an irresponsible decision does not bring credit to the administration. In his statement, Umesh Naik described Adarsha Hospital as a reputed healthcare institution in Udupi district and highlighted Dr Chandrashekar's contributions to medical and social service for over 30 years. He said the institution has been a source of hope for the underprivileged through its continued healthcare and social initiatives. He termed the decision to announce Dr Chandrashekar's name for the prestigious award and subsequently remove it citing a technical error as unfortunate and unjustified. Withdrawing an award after its announcement amounts to an insult not only to the individual concerned but also to the wider community that recognises and respects his contributions, he said. Umesh Naik urged the state government to take the matter seriously, rectify the injustice and re-announce the Rajyotsava Award in Dr Chandrashekar's name in recognition of his longstanding service. The demand for reinstating the award has gained attention in Udupi, with calls growing for the government to correct the alleged administrative error and recognise Dr Chandrashekar's three decades of dedicated service. title: "They really are the champions": GS Caltex, "Silva-Kwon Min-ji-Tanacha erupt for 51 points" to rout Korea Expressway Corporation in a sweep [Jangchung on-site review] - 스타뉴스
content:
They truly were the defending champions. Seoul GS Caltex announced a strong start toward their pursuit of a second consecutive title. On the 31st, at Jangchung Gymnasium in Jung-gu, Seoul, GS Caltex defeated Gimcheon Korea Expressway Corporation by a set score of 3-0 (25-18, 25-21, 25-22) in the opening match of the 2026-2027 HK Hyeongguk Life V-League women's division. Defending champion GS Caltex won the Cup Tournament and secured a pleasant victory in the opener, proving their status as the top favorite for the championship. GS Caltex started the first set with outside hitter Tanacha Suksoth (registered name: Tanacha), middle blocker Oh Se-yeon, opposite spiker Giselle Silva (registered name: Silva), outside hitter Kwon Min-ji, middle blocker Choi Ga-eun, and setter Kim Ji-won. The liberos were Han Su-jin and Choi Yoon-young. Korea Expressway Corporation countered with outside hitter Park Jeong-a, middle blocker Kim Hyeon-ji, opposite spiker Leticia Moma Basoko (registered name: Moma), outside hitter Uchiseto Mami (registered name: Mami), middle blocker Kim Se-bin, and setter Kim Da-eun. The libero was Moon Jeong-won. GS Caltex took the lead from the start. Led by Silva, who won the Most Valuable Player (MVP) award last season, Kwon Min-ji launched powerful attacks on the opposite side, while service aces from Oh Se-yeon and Kim Ji-won rattled Korea Expressway Corporation. Setter Kim Ji-won exploited the fact that the opposing blocking and defense were focused on Silva, utilizing not only Kwon Min-ji and Tanacha on the left but also central attacks and time-difference plays to trouble the Korea Expressway Corporation defense. GS Caltex's offense was not overly concentrated on Silva alone, but when blocked, they found solutions through her. In the first set, Silva scored 8 points solo, while Kwon Min-ji added 6 points and Tanacha contributed 4. Choi Ga-eun and Oh Se-yeon each added a blocking point, contributing 3 and 2 points respectively, as GS Caltex successfully seized the initiative with diverse attacking routes. Conversely, Korea Expressway Corporation, whose strengths lie in serve reception and defense, struggled to generate momentum aside from Moma, who scored 8 points solo. Their reception efficiency was 33.33%, significantly trailing GS Caltex (55.56%), which led to a decline in attacking efficiency. The situation did not change much in the second set. After assigning only 35.14% of their attacks to Silva in the first set, GS Caltex increased her share to 46.15% in the second set, and Silva led the offense by scoring 11 points solo. Silva also added blocking and service aces to press Korea Expressway Corporation. With the team leading 19-13, Yoo Seo-yeon was substituted in for Tanacha. Subsequently, Silva scored 4 points and forced one defensive error from the opponent, securing the second set for GS Caltex. Korea Expressway Corporation started the third set by substituting outside hitter Kang So-hwi for Park Jeong-a, and their defensive stability improved significantly, launching a counterattack. However, GS Caltex began to close in as well. In particular, during the longest rally of the day, setter Kim Ji-won finished an attack with a two-step hit, pressuring Korea Expressway Corporation. Following this, Tanacha recorded a diagonal attack and a block, and Silva's high-altitude bombardment tied the set for the first time. title: 'Yoo Soo-yeon's Return' and Champion GS Caltex: Lee Young-tak's 'Happy Dilemma' ... Kim Young-rae, Korea Expressway Corporation Head Coach, in Debut Match: "I'm Very Nervous, but I Will Support the Players" [Jangchung On-Site Report] - 스타뉴스
content:
The opening match of the 2026-2027 HK Huhguk Financial V-League Women's Division. Defending champions Seoul GS Caltex met Gimcheon Korea Expressway Corporation, which is starting anew with a new head coach. The teams are set for another fierce battle, following their encounter in the Cup tournament final. GS Caltex Head Coach Lee Young-tak (49) met with reporters ahead of the season opener against Korea Expressway Corporation, scheduled to begin at 4 p.m. on the 31st at Jangchung Gymnasium in Jung-gu, Seoul. "We earned the right to host the opening match after winning last season's championship. While there is pressure, I believe the players will handle it well," he said. The team is riding high momentum after topping the Cup tournament, and another positive development has emerged: outside hitter Yoo Soo-yeon has returned from injury. She is expected to double the team's offensive firepower alongside Kwon Min-ji, who delivered a stunning performance in the Cup tournament. "Both players have different strengths and weaknesses, so figuring out how to combine them effectively is a concern," Head Coach Lee said. "However, it is a happy dilemma to think about who to put on the court because we have plenty of options, rather than worrying about not having enough players." He added, "During training, I plan to prioritize playing those who are in good condition or showing strong performance. Yoo Soo-yeon completed her rehabilitation well and has been training with us continuously since the KOVO Cup ended. Her condition has improved significantly, and there is no issue with putting her into a match." They faced Korea Expressway Corporation, which won a close five-set match in the Cup tournament. The team also lost to them in the group stage, making them a difficult opponent. "We lost once and won once against Korea Expressway Corporation in the Cup tournament, but they are well-organized and have solid performance, so I think today will be a tough game," Head Coach Lee said. "Since we won our last match and carried that momentum positively, I hope the players show confidence on the court, just like they did in the final." Breaking through their solid receiving line is a key challenge. "If we can disrupt their serve reception with our serves, the game becomes easier to play," Head Coach Lee said. "However, their receiving line and defense are so solid that they handle even powerful serves well. Rather than hitting hard serves and risking errors, we plan to target specific spots and lengths. There are definitely points of attack even without relying solely on hard serves." Kim Young-rae (45), Korea Expressway Corporation Head Coach, who was promoted from acting head coach to the official position two days before the opener, said, "I am very tense, but also excited. We have prepared well, so I need to help the players perform their best. I am much more nervous than during my debut as acting head coach. The first step is the most important. This is not only the first game of the season but also my first as a head coach. I trust the players and will support them well." The goal is to play solid, well-organized volleyball. "We must avoid silly errors," Head Coach Kim said. "When young players come in and cannot receive or set the ball because they are not in their proper positions, the team's atmosphere sinks. We have talked a lot about this. Moon Jung-won does an excellent job of stabilizing the center. I trust that, but when young players make silly errors, it kills the momentum." He added, "I want to build a team that never gives up. A passionate team—both in how fans see us and in our own spirit. Creating a tenacious team is a major task." <© STARNEWS. All rights reserved. A handlebar raised 0.6 inches, footpegs lowered 0.8 inches, and a slimmer tank and tail make the GS feel like a big dirt bike when standing. The 34.3-inch seat height is tall; optional Rallye seats lower it 1.4 inches or raise it 0.8 inches. The 895cc parallel twin from the F 900 R and F 900 XR makes 105 horsepower and 69 ft-lbs of torque, 10 horsepower more than the 850. A 270/450-degree firing order gives it a pleasant throb instead of a buzz, and the GS is stable and comfortable on long freeway stints. A fully adjustable 43mm Showa inverted fork and a ZF shock with rebound damping and hydraulic spring-preload adjustment provide about nine inches of travel at each end. The suspension is compliant without being soft and stays balanced off-road. The $1495 Enduro Package Pro adds a fully adjustable 45mm Showa fork, a fully adjustable Sachs ZF shock, and a taller handlebar. Twin 305mm front discs with two-piston Brembo calipers have a soft initial bite that suits the dirt. Road and Rain ride modes are standard. The $1750 Premium Package adds Dynamic, Enduro, and Enduro Pro modes, a quickshifter, cruise control, keyless ride, GPS prep, and tire-pressure monitoring. Enduro Pro is the dirt mode, with strong, linear throttle response, minimal traction control, and front-only ABS. title: Bullish Options Trades Slow amid AI Uncertainty - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Options markets are showing signs of increased nervousness about artificial intelligence (AI) as investors focus closely on earnings from large tech companies and try to separate likely winners from losers, says Lee Coppersmith from the Equity Derivative Sales team in Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities. Overall demand for AI stocks remains strong and the S&P has remained resilient, but put option buying has picked up in recent weeks while activity has waned in call options that would reward a jump in equities, he explains on The Markets podcast. Chris Hussey: This is The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey, and today is Thursday, October 29th, and I'm here on the Goldman Sachs trading floor with Lee Coppersmith, who is on our hedge fund derivative sales desk within FICC and Equities. And we're going to be talking about everything that's current right now, the Fed, earnings, AI, the retail investors, vol, the whole shebang. Lee, thanks so much for joining us. Chris Hussey: Okay, Lee, let's start with the Fed, one of the big pieces of news that came out this week. What did we learn? What was the market's reaction? Lee Coppersmith: So stepping back, I think when you look at the setup heading into the Fed, the S&P options market was implying somewhere between a 60 and 65 basis point move. That's a bit lower than we've seen going into the previous FOMC meetings, somewhere around, call it 75 basis points. So I think the focus on the Fed was actually kind of like secondhand relative to the earnings that we're kind of digesting around it. Mainly, I think this is because you weren't really expecting a decision from them yesterday. So overall, I think Warsh and the committee struck this balanced tone, but there was a little bit of apprehension, I think, in the way they conveyed their message, particularly around the correlation between interest rates and the AI story, which I think kind of suggested they are happy to go at a slower pace. The equity markets actually digested this all very well. This was the first time in seven meetings that the S&P actually finished up on the day after an FOMC press conference. So I think all things considered, it was a sigh of relief after we've seen multiple press conferences in a row inject some kind of volatility into the equity space. Chris Hussey: Well, it's always great to get a little bit of a sigh of relief. Let's go to the earnings side then, because maybe that's not quite the sigh of relief. Obviously, the AI trade very much in focus across earnings. High bar for growth. We're in the heart of it right now. What are we seeing? How do you feel about the sustainability of everything? Lee Coppersmith: So, so far you've seen a mixed bag. I think the implied moves heading into this earnings season were all roughly fair, about in line with recent averages over the last few quarters. The main takeaway for us is that AI demand remains incredibly strong, but the competition has become more fierce, and so the dispersion around the market's reaction has increased a lot. We saw that yesterday with the two mega cap tech companies. We've seen that over the last, call it, month, both in the US, across Korea, and even in Europe. So I think the bottom line for us is that there's not really much poking at the AI demand story, but there's a lot more focus around the financing and who's the winner and loser going forward. Chris Hussey: All right. I want to touch on that financing side, because there was a little bit of a credit wobble earlier in the month. What do you think about that? Do you see that in the equity option side, these types of credit wobbles? Lee Coppersmith: So, the credit market to us has been very concentrated to the spaces that have much more AI exposure. If you look at the other spaces within credit, they've all been relatively more insulated or contained in terms of the price moves. The equity space has been incredibly great at essentially migrating some of the volatility to only specific pockets. S&P only really drew down two and a half percent, call it peak to trough. So I think within credit, again, back to this point around who's going to fund this AI build-out, that's the main focus. And when you think about the amount of issuance so far in 2026, it's about three times higher than it was in 2025. And so I think the full story as it relates to credit is this supply versus demand story is getting way more over-tilted towards supply versus demand, and I think that's really the kind of main story here that's kind of leading to wider credit spreads. Chris Hussey: It's been an interesting dynamic, though, because one of the sort of lessons of the post-pandemic equity boom has been that demand has always kept up with supply, no matter where you've been. In fact, demand has led supply. So it'll be interesting to see how that plays out. One of the elements of demand that has been an interesting part of the AI trade has been the retail investor. In June in particular, you saw a lot of demand there sort of pushing a lot of the mega cap tech trade up. Where's that retail investor now? Were they flushed out? Lee Coppersmith: So retail activity has cooled. I wouldn't say that they've completely abandoned the AI trade or the market as a whole, but if you look at volumes today on average versus where we were in late June, volumes from the retail community are down roughly, call it, 20%. So I think what you're saying right now is essentially the sponsorship has waned a little bit because the excitement around the right tail distribution has come in. The same way we've seen our institutional client base buy less call options, we're seeing the same thing happen with retail essentially. So, the one area where we are still seeing some dip buying has been in the leveraged ETF space. Those volumes remain pretty strong. But in terms of the options market, we're not seeing the same type of call buying activity that we once were. Chris Hussey: So if we have this decline in call buying activity, we have this decline in the options market in terms of demand, I would imagine that's pretty good for the price of options. What are you seeing in terms of the hedging community? Are they sort of diving in and taking advantage of this? Lee Coppersmith: Yeah, I think when you kind of back up, the main story for most of this year has been buying calls for sure and people trying to play for this explosive right tail distribution. Really since the end of the summer, most of the pullback in implied volatility, the way the options market's pricing distributions, has mainly been because people have been taking risk down more so on the call option side, not because of put buying. What's happened more recently in the last, call it, few weeks, is we have seen this debate become more two-sided and put buying has picked up, which tells us there's a lot more nervousness around just how things will play out between now through year-end. To us, though, when you think about what the market's implying, the distributions are now pretty fair on both ends. And so because the absolute level of vol isn't very high, we actually think it's a pretty good time to be deploying capital through the options market to be expressing these between now through year-end just because the catalyst path is so rich. Chris Hussey: Is there any risk that we have sort of a self-fulfilling prophecy, though, here? As the market stays flat or drifts a little lower, there's no sort of reward for having bought calls and so you start buying puts and it just, you know, so the more the market is flat, the worse the options market is. Lee Coppersmith: There is definitely a case to be made around that. I think what we've seen now is we've been in this amazingly large consolidation pattern at the index level. However, under the surface, things are realizing. And so, the main theme that we've seen continue to resonate in our world in the option space has been dispersion. Now, it's completely evolved from where we were, call it, in Q1 and Q2 of this year, mainly because you had the momentum factor working on a really high sharp. What's happened really since then is that the momentum factor itself has seen a lot more dispersion. And so like everything else this year, we've just seen, again, a new trend take place where you have to get even more surgical with the way you think about implementing any of your exposure through options particularly. Chris Hussey: Yeah, that seems to be the theme of this conversation here, right? We have dispersion in fundamentals as competition picks up in the AI trade, and we have dispersion in the market that is helping to play that. Okay, put a bow on it. What's the trade? Lee Coppersmith: I think the easiest place to go hunt right now is particularly outside of the AI space. We like biotech here. Lee Coppersmith: We think it's a space that offers a lot of secular properties, just like some of the AI trades previously. But now there's this window where you could potentially have a tailwind of lower rates, more M&A, and I do think the added layer of maybe more drug discovery going forward as a result of some of these AI companies could help lend itself to having more capital get attracted to that area. Chris Hussey: Lee, terrific. Always a wealth of information. Really appreciate you joining us. Chris Hussey: Before I go, I want to make one comment. 45 years ago, I discovered that my mother had breast cancer. Since that time, my family has rallied around Breast Cancer Awareness Month, which comes every October, to help raise money for a cure. You've seen me wear pink throughout October. I encourage everybody to go out there, support breast cancer awareness, and the research that's working towards a cure. That does it for this week's episode of The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey. Thanks for listening. title: The Outlook for US Housing in 2027 amid Rising Mortgage Rates - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Rising mortgage rates are likely to outweigh a longstanding housing shortage in the US next year, leading to a drop in both the sales of existing homes and the construction of new ones, according to Goldman Sachs Research. “In 2027, we expect the headwind from affordability to increasingly dominate, weighing further on activity,” economists Ronnie Walker and David Mericle write in a report. They project that existing home sales will total just 3.9 million in 2027, modestly below their forecast of 4 million for 2026 but 26% below 2019 levels. Against the backdrop of slower home sales, they forecast another year of “anemic” home price growth: 0.8% December-over-December in 2027 after 1.1% in 2026 and 1.2% in 2025. Borrowing costs are a key component of housing affordability. This year’s jump in mortgage rates—in response to the Iran War, higher oil prices, and the prospect of rate hikes by the Federal Reserve—has reduced incentives for homeowners to sell. More than 95% of mortgage borrowers have interest rates below current market rates, and 65% have rates two percentage points below market rates, creating a “lock-in” effect that is slowing sales. In order to purchase a new home, such homebuyers would need to prepay their current mortgage and take out a new mortgage at a higher rate. “The combination of mortgage borrowers refinancing at low rates en masse in 2020 and 2021 and the high current level of mortgage rates has created a significant financial cost to moving,” Walker and Mericle write. Rates for 30-year mortgages in the US have climbed to 7.32% (as of October 22). Goldman Sachs Research’s credit strategists expect mortgage rates to decline in 2027 but remain elevated at 6.4%. Even if that decline is realized, affordability will remain at historically poor levels. Beyond next year, Goldman Sachs Research expects existing home sales to gradually edge higher, reflecting the natural decay of the lock-in effect that comes from, for example, borrowers paying down their mortgages. The renewed popularity of adjustable-rate mortgages in the post-pandemic period could theoretically accelerate this process as well. As rates on such mortgages reset, they tend to erode the impact of the lock-in effect, as seen in other countries where adjustable-rate mortgages are more prevalent. But that impact is likely to be modest in the US, especially over the next couple of years. Adjustable-rate mortgages represent less than 10% of all outstanding mortgages in the US, and only a small share of them will begin to reset in the coming years. Housing activity as measured by residential fixed investment (RFI)—a component of gross domestic product that includes new home construction—is likely to begin recovering by next summer after an expected decline in the months ahead. After posting an estimated 3.1% annualized increase in this year’s third quarter, RFI is forecast to contract by 2.5%, 4%, and 1% annualized in the three quarters that follow, respectively. Thereafter, our researchers expect activity to rebound to a 1-2% growth pace starting in the second half of next year, reflecting the impact of declining mortgage rates. If rates remain at current levels instead, that would lower their RFI growth forecasts by one to two percentage points through the end of 2027. The longstanding housing shortage has kept single-family homebuilding resistant to higher interest rates. Single-family starts have averaged 3% higher than above 2019 levels despite mortgage rates that are three-and-a-half percentage points higher today. This year, however, they have declined by 3% compared with last year, and the slippage is likely to continue. Goldman Sachs Research expects single-family starts to total 0.87 million in 2027 compared to an estimated 0.90 million in 2026. Our economists point to the increase in the available supply of housing, as well as the corresponding compression of margins for homebuilders back to pre-pandemic levels. The elevated pace of homebuilding in recent years has eased historically tight supply-and-demand balances. When the available supply of housing improves, it tends to increase homebuilders’ sensitivity to affordability constraints. Prior analysis by Goldman Sachs Research shows that the higher the vacancy rate was the year before, the more sensitive housing starts are to mortgage rate increases. The combination of still-solid supply growth and slightly weaker demand should push the homeowner vacancy rate higher in the months ahead, from 1.2% in this year’s second quarter to 1.4% by the fourth quarter of 2027. Housing demand is being buoyed by domestic demographic trends that remain supportive, along with real income growth that is likely to accelerate next year, and “build-to-rent” housing, which typically involves a partnership between single-family rental companies and homebuilders to construct rental homes. But on the negative side, survey-based measures of purchase intentions have declined in recent months. Our economists also expect that reduced immigration will continue to weigh on household formation. “We expect housing demand to remain tepid,” Walker and Mericle write. The 2026-2027 V-League season kicks off, marking the start of a six-month journey for professional volleyball, the crown jewel of winter sports. The men’s division begins with a match between Korean Air and Hyundai Capital, while the women’s division opens with a game between GS Caltex and Korea Expressway Corporation on October 31. This season’s men’s division is expected to feature a two-horse race between last season’s championship finalists, Korean Air and Hyundai Capital, with the remaining five teams challenging for supremacy. Korean Air retains key players Han Sunsoo, Jeong Jiseok, and Im Donghyuk, while Hyundai Capital has secured core assets Heo Su-bong and Hwang Seungbin. Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO), equipped with setter Lee Mingyu, Asian quota player Usman (Pakistan), and foreign player Sho (Canada), is considered a potential contender to these top two. The challenges posed by Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance and KB Insurance are also noteworthy. Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance has appointed Tommi Tiilikainen, Finland, as their new head coach, who previously led Korean Air to three consecutive unified championships. KB Insurance is helmed by Isanaye Ramires, Brazil, the former coach of the South Korean men’s national volleyball team. The women’s division is anticipated to be a fierce battle, with GS Caltex, the reigning champions and cup tournament winners, holding a slight advantage. GS Caltex, featuring the dynamic duo of Silva, Cuba, and Tanacha, Thailand, will face challenges from Korea Expressway Corporation, led by Moma, Cameroon, and Park Jeongah; Jung Hoyoung and Pyo Seungjoo of Heungkuk Life Insurance; and Hyundai Engineering & Construction, which has signed Mega, Indonesia, the player who spearheaded the Jung Kwan Jang phenomenon from 2023 to 2025 amid the void left by the retired Yang Hyo-jin. The Korea Volleyball Federation (KOVO) has decided to adopt the FIVB global regulations for line in/out readings starting this season. Instead of the previously complex local rules, any contact between the ball and the line at the moment it touches the floor will now be ruled as ‘in.’

title: This Used Lexus Has A 467-HP V8 And Costs Half Of Its Original MSRP - Top Speed
content: You wouldn’t know it by their current lineup, but Lexus used to be the king of sedans. They actually started their brand with a full-size luxury limousine, the Lexus LS. Then, dealers called on Lexus to give them a slightly more accessible, reasonably priced sedan. Lexus responded with the ES. Then, in 1991, Toyota wanted a luxury sedan similar to Italian luxury sedans for their domestic market in Japan. It was originally dubbed the Toyota Aristo. It was such a hit that by 1993, it moved to selling internationally with a name badge switch to the GS 300. By the early to mid-2010s, the Lexus GS had already hit icon status and was a cult hit among auto enthusiasts. From the start, it was available with either a six-cylinder or a more powerful V8 engine. While there doesn’t seem to be any announced new version of the now venerated GS coming back anytime soon, there is still a lot of interest in the used market. While things are heading in the direction of electrification and turbocharged power, the GS still offers analog capabilities that the market is still looking for. We’re going to go over the necessary things to look out for if you’re interested in this future classic. First and foremost, the Lexus GS F is a luxury sedan. We already know that. The GS F is not only luxurious but also a powerful brute, predicated on its now nearly extinct powertrain. While the United States market only received an inline six-cylinder engine that made 220 horsepower, the rest of the world was already getting the V8. We received the first generation V8 here by 1998. These, however, were just regular luxury sedans with a big V8. They weren't necessarily "F" standard and didn't have any of the performance features you would come to expect. The second generation was the first Lexus GS to technically get the “F” treatment, even if it wasn’t referred to as such. That moniker belongs to the 2016 model and later. You could still get a V8 in the GS 460 from 2008 to 2011, but it wasn’t nearly as powerful. The 2016 to 2020 model is where the true power lies, as it’s tied to a massive naturally aspirated 5.0-liter V8 that outputs an impressive 467 horsepower and 389 pound-feet of torque. Even more impressive is its reported zero to 60 MPH time of just 4.4 seconds. This is also a high-revving engine that can achieve 7,100 RPM. The Lexus “F” badge on any Lexus represents the legendary Fuji Speedway in Japan. With that in mind, Lexus pulls out all the technological stops to give it the best quality sport handling you would come to expect from a mid-size sport limo. Tethered to the V8 is an eight-speed Sport Direct Shift automatic transmission that also has a manual mode. As you’d probably expect, this also has RWD, but what you might not expect is that it’s equipped with a torque vectoring differential. This allows you to choose from Standard, Slalom, and Track modes. Finally, there are Brembo brakes, a multi-link rear suspension with adaptive dampers, and a double wishbone suspension. Music to our ears. Typically, within the first five years of any mid-size luxury sedan, they lose between 45 and 60 percent of their original MSRP value. Basic economics suggest that the market just doesn’t want mid-size luxury sedans. Everybody wants an SUV, in the US at least. It's even evident in the fact that Mercedes-AMG just released their first-ever GT SUV. Sport variants of any vehicle typically hold their value slightly more than their standard counterparts, but the market is still not entirely there for luxury sedans. You would, however, be shocked to see how well the GS F holds its value. While other sedans are losing their value at a steep decline in five years, a 2016 model, for example, still retains about 44 percent of its original value, according to Kelley Blue Book. The 2018 and 2020 models aren’t that far off either, with 2018 at 48 and 2020 at 55 percent respectively. If we were to follow that same order, the original MSRPs were $85,345 to $86,035 max. Now, they're valued between $41,800 and $47,100 depending on the year, mileage, condition, and the like. It’s ended up (in the American market at least) mainly competing with the likes of the BMW M5 and Mercedes-AMG E63. Other competitors for the regular sedan include the Audi A6. If we’re talking pricing, Kelley Blue Book puts the 2018 BMW M5 at about $41,500 give or take. The AMG E63 of the same year is around $57,770, even closer to $49,000. Both the Mercedes and the BMW have more power and better traction with all-wheel drive, but the Lexus GS F has a naturally aspirated 5.0-liter V8 that most enthusiasts want. Most enthusiasts want that 5.0-liter naturally aspirated V8 because of the simplicity it offers from a maintenance standpoint. Not only that, but at the end of the day, it is considered a Toyota and is often viewed as more reliable from a maintenance standpoint. Not to take away from the Lexus brand itself, because as a standalone, it has achieved the number one spot on JD Power’s most reliable brand list for years and years. At the end of the day, however, this is still a sport sedan, and you will have to pay Sport Sedan pricing for maintenance. Repair pal suggests that the Lexus GS F shows an annual maintenance cost of around $499. This, of course, is dependent on how much you drive it, or whether you actually end up tracking it, as performance tires are often more expensive. That number of $499 also seems awfully low considering this is a more special edition than your standard model. This thing is also heavy at a curb weight of 4,034 pounds. That means you'll be changing the Brembo brakes more frequently. Be sure to ask wherever you're buying this from for a complete maintenance history, especially regarding oil changes and spark plug replacements.​​​​​​​ Although this might be a Lexus, that doesn’t mean that it comes without issues. There was a fuel pump recall for the 2016 to 2018 models, so be sure to check the VIN to confirm whether the recall was addressed or whether it affected that specific model at all. Some blog websites have reported that the carbon fiber trim has lost some of its clear coat as well. The price points for this specific model can vary wildly. You also shouldn’t necessarily buy the newest and lowest mileage one, as maintenance plays a huge role in the quality of your GS F. We’ve even seen some on Cars.com that are going for $70,000 to $90,000. If you find a model in that price range, you could also opt for the newer IS 500, which also has a 5.0-liter naturally aspirated V8. However, you might not necessarily want that, as the cabin is much more cramped. The Lexus GS offers more space, comfort, and convenience. We want to hear from you. Information that may have been exposed includes the names, nicknames, dates of birth, mobile phone numbers, gender, email addresses, addresses, membership numbers, residence types, passwords, administrator IDs, household head status, signup dates and times, last login internet protocol (IP) addresses, and RF card numbers of residents who use the system. GS Engineering & Construction reported the incident to the relevant authorities immediately after recognizing it, and the exact scale of damage and scope of the leak is under investigation. title: This WNBA Finals stat is good omen for Valkyries in Game 7 against Dream - ClutchPoints
content: The Valkyries have WNBA history on their side coming into the deciding Game 7 of the Finals against the Dream. The Golden State Valkyries came into Game 6 looking to close out the WNBA Finals and secure the franchise’s first championship, but they were blitzed by the Atlanta Dream, 80-69, and thus, will have to play in a winner takes all Game 7 on Saturday. However, the Valkyries might have a little history on their side. Coming into this series, there have been 13 times in WNBA history where the Finals have come down to a deciding game. The team with homecourt advantage has won 11 of those Finals series, as per Alexa Philippou of ESPN. This will be the 14th WNBA Finals to come down to a winner takes all game, and that stat certainly bodes well for the Valkyries against the Dream. Game 7 of the 2026 WNBA Finals will be held at Chase Center, the home arena of the Valkyries. During the playoffs this season, they are 6-1 on their home court with their sole loss coming to the Dream in Game 2 of this Finals series. This is also going to be the second time in the last three seasons that the WNBA Finals has come down to the final game of the series, as per Philippou. Although the league only switched to a best-of-seven format last year, in 2024, the New York Liberty defeated the Minnesota Lynx, 3-2, when it was still a best-of-five series. No matter who wins the series on Saturday, it will be the first title in franchise history for both teams. The Valkyries are only in their second year of existence as an expansion team, while the Dream have reached the WNBA Finals in 2010, 2011 and 2013 but were unable to cross the finish line. title: Dissolve GCC council if you want to ignore elected reps: Mayor R Priya - The New Indian Express
content: CHENNAI: “Ungaluku ellam oru prachanai na indha MLA kita varringa, enake oru prachanai na naan yaar kita poven?” A popular Tamil film comedy dialogue that roughly translates to “When you have a problem, you come to this MLA, when I have a problem, who do I go to?” found an unlikely parallel in the Chennai Corporation council meeting on Thursday, when Mayor R Priya said she, too, was being left out of the loop by government officials. The exchange began with councillors complaining that officials were failing to invite them to inaugurations and inspections, many of which were attended by TVK MLAs or ministers. Priya said she was facing the same problem, citing the lack of communication about Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay’s visit timings. “You’re all saying officials aren’t calling you for inaugurations or other events, but the truth is I’m in the same situation,” she said. Deputy Mayor M Magesh Kumaar said that the Mayor went to meet PM as the timings were informed but was not the case with CM. Priya said, “If the CM is coming, will I just sit in Ripon Buildings from morning to night? They have to tell me the CM’s arrival time for me to be present, which has not been communicated at all. It is not me ignoring the government, but the government ignoring the mayor.” Shr questioned why councillors were being ignored. The discussion also touched on the format prescribed by the directorate of information and public relations for plaques at inaugurated projects, with councillors objecting to it, reiterating the sidelining of elected representatives. She also said that the state could dissolve the council if it wants to sideline elected representatives. The GCC commissioner, G S Sameeran, agreed that elected representatives should be invited to such events, except during surprise inspections. title: GS Engineering & Construction posts profit drop as plant gains offset housing slump - Chosunbiz
content: Plant wins cushion earnings as housing softness and lower sales weigh GS Engineering & Construction said on the 30th that operating profit for the third quarter came in at 95.5 billion won. That was down 35.7% from the same period a year earlier (148.5 billion won). Revenue fell 14.5% to 2.7442 trillion won. By business division, revenue was as follows: ▲ architecture and dwellings division 1.4997 trillion won ▲ infrastructure division 343.7 billion won ▲ plant division 457 billion won. Plant division revenue rose 34.6% from a year earlier as large domestic and overseas projects got fully underway. In contrast, due to a decrease in dwellings supply volume, revenue at the architecture and dwellings division fell 18.7% over the same period. GS Engineering & Construction said, "We supplied about 13,000 dwellings through the third quarter this year, and once these projects move into full swing, revenue will turn upward." New orders in the third quarter totaled 3.9584 trillion won. The architecture and dwellings division won contracts such as the Yongsan Munbae-dong mixed-use residential and commercial complex (571.7 billion won) and the Namyangju Wangsuk 2 A8, 12BL private-participation project (217.3 billion won). The infrastructure division secured new orders such as the Section 3 construction of the Second Gyeongchun National Highway (Namyangju–Chuncheon) (104.3 billion won). Danwood, a modular-focused subsidiary located in Poland, recorded 196.2 billion won in new orders. Construction rights secured for urban renewal project sites through the third quarter this year amount to about 5.5 trillion won. A GS Engineering & Construction official said, "We expect to secure multiple construction rights for redevelopment projects at major, high-profit sites in Seoul, including Mok-dong Complex 12 and Yeouido Eunha and Samik Apartments, and we expect new orders to increase further going forward."
